feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads polished and modern, but it is slightly repetitive and could be tightened to sharpen impact and reduce overlap across skills, projects, and experience.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale indicators and concrete platforms/tools: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” GA4, BigQuery, Drupal, etc.  
- Writing is generally clean, professional, and credible, with a strong match between headline, competencies, and work history.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” repeat similar themes. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially for the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost savings).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in bullets, and “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma. No major misspellings or typos found; grammar is strong overall.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more outcome-oriented: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years modernizing public-sector web ecosystems, governance, and content operations for high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”
- Add 1–2 scale markers from recent roles to increase impact, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace the generic “Leads…” list with a more distinctive positioning statement: “Combines platform strategy, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia operations to improve discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”
- Consider “AI-enabled search and content experiences” instead of broader “AI-enabled user experiences” for specificity and consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- The current intro repeats the subtitle and much of the Core Competencies list.
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered elsewhere; keep the intro focused on platform leadership and transformation.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive capability areas and used more parallel, concise phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use tighter, noun-led phrasing for consistency: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Consider replacing “content experiences” with “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Change “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to sound more senior and strategic.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “editorial systems” vs. “livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6 items or making it more distinct from those sections.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills’ “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a concise bullet for easier scanning.
- Use parallel, action-led phrasing: “Launched,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Produced,” rather than repeating “Designed/Built/Developed.”
- Increase specificity where possible with scale or audience impact, especially for the microsite, anniversary campaign, and video series.
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with your current freelance role and NACo experience; keep this block brief and project-focused rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “web features,” and “distribution across website, email and social channels” echo existing CV language and could be condensed.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground outcomes, scale, and flagship work so it feels distinct from the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, strengthening enterprise communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/governance/operations into one sharper line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination, publishing consistency, and decision-making.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign bullet outcome-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users, teams enabled, turnaround reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements, or adoption of the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo governance language; use this item to emphasize consulting impact and current AI/search work.
- The microsite and AI-search bullets partially duplicate Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level and let the project section carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It will be even stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with an outcome-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Condense channel oversight bullets and lead with the biggest wins: website migration, analytics stack, and in-house studio build.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: email list size/open rates, social growth/engagement, video output, reporting time saved, or governance adoption across teams.
- Possible rewrite:
- Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.
- Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio and expanded capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content.
- Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting; formalized publishing governance and cross-department planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital channels” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version more strategic than operational.
- Video-program growth also appears in earlier NACo entries; emphasize studio build and enterprise capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more role-specific by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” and “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” with direct ownership where accurate: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.”
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep the emphasis here on scaling/operationalizing it, not originating it.
- “editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director role; avoid broad governance language better reserved for the more senior position.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and heavily overlaps with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixed styles like “leadership” vs. “messaging.”
- Consider swapping “multi-channel” for “cross-channel” or “integrated” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, move impact proof to experience bullets rather than listing broad skills here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery
- CMS modernization and migration
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint, Power Pages and Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- Drop “jQuery” unless required by target roles; it reads dated versus your recent leadership profile.
- Put Drupal first and group WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages as secondary platforms to reflect recency and strongest evidence.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web platforms” or “public-sector web platforms” to reinforce scale and context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” repeats Core Competencies and recent project content.
- Most tools here duplicate the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version more strategic, less exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership rather than repeating tool names already listed elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and insight generation using GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Put the most strategic items first: KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, analytics strategy, then platforms.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “for enterprise web performance and content optimization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider shortening this section or using it to highlight interpretation/decision support, not just tools.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing operational leadership over task-level production.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Operations & Event Production**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event operations
- In-house studio buildout and production workflows
- PTZ camera systems and multi-camera direction
- If space allows, swap one bullet for a stronger scope signal: **Virtual, hybrid and on-site event delivery**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is covered by Technical + IT tools (Premiere Pro, Audition) and several work-experience bullets; avoid repeating tool-level phrasing here.
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate Core Competencies; use this section to show depth/seniority instead.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” In this section, make it more implementation-focused and emphasize the most relevant platform first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers only where defensible, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, sharpen scope: **CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Best upgrade: replace one lower-value item with a stronger, evidenced platform/version from recent work if accurate, e.g. **Drupal 10** instead of generic Drupal

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Topline Skills” entry **Web Platforms & Technical Execution** almost exactly; consider keeping platforms here and removing them from Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Rewrite as: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • API and tag-management integrations • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal front-end components,” “deployed automation via GitHub Actions,” or “implemented GTM-based tracking.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you specifically want this section limited to implementation tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to grouped, capability-led phrasing: “Workflow automation & collaboration: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team operations: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If true, add light context instead of only names: “used to build editorial planning systems, automate handoffs/notifications, and coordinate cross-team publishing.”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value tools if space is tight; Slack/Teams are expected and add less differentiation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them verbatim across sections.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was meaningfully used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. It should also align more clearly with the candidate’s recent leadership in email/newsletter operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, member communications)_
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: add a parenthetical such as **supporting newsletters to tens of thousands of recipients** or **used for high-volume advocacy/member communications**
- Keep platform names only once; use this line for tools, and leave strategy/operations detail to work experience bullets

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email/newsletter bullets; avoid repeating campaign-management language here
- If Dynamics 365 was only lightly used, consider dropping it to keep this list credible and focused

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to signal depth beyond platform names. Tightening the phrasing and adding higher-value capability language would make it feel less repetitive.

Suggested edit
- Replace with: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • SEO analysis • Experimentation
- Put the strongest, most strategic tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio.
- Swap generic “Dashboarding” for “KPI reporting” or “Executive reporting” to better match seniority.
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation” only if you’ve directly run tests; otherwise remove it to avoid overstating.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one more tool-focused while leaving the other outcomes/capability-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director of Digital Media role, so avoid repeating all five elsewhere unless needed for ATS.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than achievement. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content production, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and video.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website traffic during refresh, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or team size supported.
- Make contributions more active and specific: “Supported a major website refresh” → “Helped deliver a major website refresh, coordinating content updates and digital production.”
- Tighten the closing clause: “Supervised and coached a digital media associate on day-to-day content production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on launching/building the program, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as early team/process foundation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the standout achievement. Since this is the oldest role, keep it concise and emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest signal of impact and progression into digital/media leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the most distinctive outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make the podcast launch the lead accomplishment: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of research/projects supported.
- Consider a one-line version to save space: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county programs and policy work; produced digital content and launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize multimedia broadly here if video/livestream growth is better documented in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
